Canberra Tracks lists regular visitor opening Tuesday to Sunday, generally 10am–4pm, but check current hours and any conservation works before travelling. This is a managed heritage attraction, not an abandoned site. Stay in visitor areas and follow site directions. Sources: https://www.canberratracks.act.gov.au/heritage-trails/track-2-the-limestone-plains/lanyon ; https://www.act.gov.au/BuiltforCBR/browse-all-projects/entertainment-arts-and-sports/lanyon-homestead

name: Calthorpes' House
area: 24 Mugga Way, Red Hill ACT — visitor access by published opening times / booking.
status: Heritage-listed 1920s house museum — managed visitor attraction
notes: Built and furnished in 1927, the house preserves the domestic setting and belongings of the Calthorpe family, who lived there until the 1980s. It is a historic house museum, not abandoned. Check the Cultural Facilities Corporation visitor information for current opening days, tours and any temporary closures before visiting. Sources: https://www.canberratracks.act.gov.au/heritage-trails/track-2-the-limestone-plains/calthorpes-house ; https://www.culturalfacilities.act.gov.au/

name: Mugga-Mugga Cottage
area: 129 Narrabundah Lane, Symonston ACT — managed heritage visitor site; check opening dates.
status: 1850s workers' cottage and heritage collection — periodic public opening
notes: A surviving workers' cottage from the Duntroon estate, with a collection associated with the Curley family, who lived there from 1913. Canberra Tracks lists public opening on the first weekend of each month, 10am–2pm; confirm current arrangements before travelling. The site also contains protected grassland and Aboriginal heritage values. Keep to visitor paths and do not disturb plants, artefacts or ground surfaces. Sources: https://www.canberratracks.act.gov.au/heritage-trails/track-7-woden-heritage-track/mugga-mugga ; https://www.act.gov.au/environment/heritage/act-heritage-register

name: Hall Village Historic Precinct
area: Victoria Street and surrounding public streets, Hall ACT — some heritage buildings are private property.
status: Historic rural village — public street heritage walk; individual sites have mixed access
notes: Hall was established as a rural village in the 1880s. Canberra Tracks describes ten interpretive signs around the village, including the former general store, school and former Kinlyside Hall; the Laurie Copping School Museum is a visitor attraction. Some buildings shown on the heritage walk are private property, so view only from public streets unless a site is officially open. Sources: https://www.canberratracks.act.gov.au/heritage-trails/track-5-gungahlin/hall-village ; https://www.canberratracks.act.gov.au/sitemap

name: Blundells Cottage
area: Wendouree Drive, Parkes ACT — public park surrounds; cottage opening/access must be checked.
status: Historic 1860s farm workers' cottage — heritage site; visitor access may be limited
notes: Built around 1860 on the Duntroon estate, Blundells Cottage is one of the last small farmhouses surviving in central Canberra. It was home to farm workers including George and Flora Blundell for almost 60 years. It is a heritage attraction rather than an abandoned building; check the National Capital Authority for current opening or tour arrangements. Do not enter when closed. Sources: https://www.canberratracks.act.gov.au/heritage-trails/track-2-the-limestone-plains/blundells-cottage ; https://www.archives.act.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0008/562544/Canberra_Research_Guide.pdf

name: Duntroon Dairy
area: Royal Military College Duntroon, Campbell ACT — controlled Defence precinct; external viewing only where permitted.
status: Early 1830s pastoral dairy — heritage building within an active Defence site
notes: The Duntroon Dairy is associated with the Campbell family's Duntroon estate and is identified by Canberra Tracks as part of the Limestone Plains heritage trail. It sits within the active Royal Military College precinct, so it is not an open urbex location. Access may be limited to authorised tours, open days or approved visitors; do not enter Defence grounds or approach security areas without permission. Sources: https://www.canberratracks.act.gov.au/heritage-trails/track-2-the-limestone-plains ; https://www.canberratracks.act.gov.au/sitemap

name: Cinema Center — Civic
area: 50 Bunda Street, Canberra City ACT 2601 — public footpaths and public-facing tenancies only.
status: Heritage-registered modernist mixed-use building — standing; not an abandoned building
notes: Designed by Enrico Taglietti, Cinema Center is a distinctive modernist building completed in the 1960s. It combined retail, offices, food venues and the former underground Center Cinema. It was registered on the ACT Heritage Register in 2021 for its architectural and cultural significance. View the exterior from public footpaths; enter only businesses or areas open to the public. The former cinema auditorium is not assumed to be publicly accessible. Sources: https://www.act.gov.au/environment/heritage/act-heritage-register ; https://www.act.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0016/2201245/2023-EA_App-E_Heritage-Impact-Assessment.pdf

name: ANZ Bank Building — Former ES&A Bank
area: Civic, Canberra City ACT 2601 — Section 3, Block 1; view from public streets only.
status: Heritage-registered historic commercial building — current internal access/use varies
notes: The former English, Scottish and Australian Bank building is listed on the ACT Heritage Register. It is an early Canberra commercial building and part of the historic Civic streetscape. This is an architectural and history stop, not a confirmed abandoned building. View from public footpaths; do not enter non-public offices or tenancies. Confirm current business access before visiting. Sources: https://www.act.gov.au/environment/heritage/act-heritage-register ; https://www.nca.gov.au/sites/default/files/2023-03/environmental_assessment_appendix_e_-_heritage_impact_assessment_0.pdf

name: Ian Potter House (Former Beauchamp House)
area: 9 Gordon Street, Acton ACT 2601 — public street frontage; interior access only for authorised events or visits.
status: Heritage-registered 1927 former hotel / residence — currently used by the Australian Academy of Science
notes: Built in 1927 as Acton Private Hotel and later known as Beauchamp House, this Inter-war Georgian Revival building is now Ian Potter House and serves as the Australian Academy of Science's administrative home. It is registered on the ACT Heritage Register. The building is in active use, not abandoned. View from public streets; interior access depends on Academy events, bookings or permission. Sources: https://www.act.gov.au/environment/heritage/act-heritage-register ; https://www.nfsa.gov.au/whats-on/our-building ; https://www.nca.gov.au/sites/default/files/2023-03/environmental_assessment_appendix_e_-_heritage_impact_assessment_0.pdf

name: Westridge House and Grounds
area: Banks Street, Yarralumla ACT — public-road viewing only; grounds/building access is not assumed.
status: 1928 heritage house within former Australian Forestry School precinct — occupied / managed property, not an abandoned site
notes: Westridge House was designed by Harold Desbrowe-Annear and completed in 1928 as the residence of the Principal of the Australian Forestry School. It is part of Canberra's early forestry and research history and has been the subject of ACT heritage registration decisions in 2026. Treat it as a heritage architecture stop only. Do not enter the grounds or building without permission; use public roads and obey all property signs. Sources: https://www.act.gov.au/environment/heritage/act-heritage-register ; https://www.finance.gov.au/government/property-and-construction/heritage-management ; https://www.act.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0008/1945880/canberra-brickworks-precinct-conservation-management-plan-2021-volume-2.pdf

name: Gungahlin Homestead and Historic Estate
area: Barton Highway, Crace ACT — general public-road vicinity only; access to the property is restricted unless officially opened.
status: Surviving 19th-century pastoral homestead — currently used by Soldier On; closed to the public
notes: Gungahlin Homestead is a surviving rural estate associated with Canberra's pastoral beginnings. The wider property later formed part of a CSIRO research campus for more than 70 years. It was provisionally registered on the ACT Heritage Register in 2026. This is a historic-building record, not a public urbex location: do not enter the homestead, grounds or research property without explicit permission. Check official heritage and land-manager notices for any public open days. Sources: https://www.act.gov.au/environment/heritage/act-heritage-register ; https://region.com.au/canberras-heritage-story-expands-with-recognition-of-capital-building-structures/1004258/ ; https://www.finance.gov.au/government/property-and-construction/heritage-management Canberra Tracks confirms Soldier On currently uses the premises and that buildings cannot be visited or viewed close up; a public sign is on Bellenden Road. Do not enter or approach the property. Checked 26 Nov 2026. Source: https://www.canberratracks.act.gov.au/heritage-trails/track-5-gungahlin/gungahlin-homestead

name: Hotel Acton (Acton House)
area: Balmain Crescent, Acton ACT 2601 — public street frontage only; interior/grounds access not assumed.
status: Heritage-registered former hotel building — standing; not confirmed abandoned
notes: Hotel Acton, also known as Acton House, is listed on the ACT Heritage Register. It is an early Canberra hotel building associated with the development of the national capital. This is a heritage architecture/history stop, not a confirmed abandoned site. View from public streets and enter only areas currently open to visitors or with permission. Check current site use and access before visiting. Source: https://www.act.gov.au/environment/heritage/act-heritage-register

name: Former Royal Canberra Hospital — Acton Peninsula Buildings
area: Acton Peninsula, Canberra ACT 2601 — public waterfront paths only; buildings and grounds may be closed or controlled.
status: Former hospital complex — heritage-listed surviving buildings; restricted access
notes: This entry covers three surviving buildings of the former Royal Canberra Hospital: Building 1 (former TB Ward), Building 2 (former Isolation Ward) and Building 15 (former Medical Superintendent's Residence). The hospital moved to its present Woden site in 1996. The buildings are individually included in the Commonwealth Heritage List and are part of the Acton Complex. They are not an open urbex site; do not enter buildings, fenced areas or work zones. View only from public paths where permitted and follow current National Capital Authority notices. Sources: https://www.nca.gov.au/planning/heritage/heritage-management-plans/acton-complex-draft-heritage-management-plan ; https://www.nca.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-04/acton_complex_draft_heritage_management_plan_2026.pdf

name: Former MLC Building — Civic
area: 161 London Circuit, Canberra City ACT 2601 — view from public footpaths only.
status: Heritage-registered former commercial office building — current use/access to be checked
notes: The Former MLC Building is listed on the ACT Heritage Register and is recognised for its place in Canberra's post-war commercial development and architectural history. This entry records the building as a heritage site, not as confirmed abandoned. View from public footpaths; do not enter offices, construction areas or private premises. Check current occupancy and redevelopment status before visiting. Source: https://www.act.gov.au/environment/heritage/act-heritage-register

name: Kingston Powerhouse Historic Precinct
area: Kingston, Canberra ACT 2604 — use public precinct paths and venue entrances; some buildings have managed/event access.
status: Heritage-registered former industrial power facility — precinct adaptively reused; not abandoned
notes: The Kingston Powerhouse Historic Precinct is listed on the ACT Heritage Register. The precinct preserves Canberra's early electricity infrastructure and includes the former powerhouse and associated industrial buildings, including the Fitters' Workshop and former Transport Depot. Some spaces are now used for arts, events and other public-facing activities. This is a heritage precinct, not an abandoned site. Use signed public areas and check individual venue opening times; do not enter closed plant rooms or restricted areas. Source: https://www.act.gov.au/environment/heritage/act-heritage-register

name: CSIRO Phytotron Building
area: Clunies Ross Street, Acton ACT 2601 — public road frontage only; CSIRO grounds/building access is restricted.
status: Historic research building — active/restricted research precinct; not an abandoned site
notes: The CSIRO Phytotron is a distinctive research facility associated with controlled-environment plant science and Canberra's research history. The ACT Heritage Register page records a previous provisional registration decision that expired; this should not be described as currently ACT-registered on that basis. The building is within a CSIRO research precinct, so access is restricted unless CSIRO authorises a visit. View only from public roads where possible; do not enter the campus or building without permission. Sources: https://www.act.gov.au/environment/heritage/act-heritage-register ; https://www.csiro.au/

name: Former Mugga Lane Zoo — Canberra Wildlife Gardens
area: Symonston — former zoo land near Mugga Lane; private property; exact address and pin withheld.
status: Former private zoo — closed around 2002; little evidence remained by 2021; redevelopment approval/review history exists; current works and condition unverified
notes: The site operated as Canberra Wildlife Gardens from 1979 and later as Mugga Lane Zoo; it closed around 2002. A 2008 local report described abandoned enclosures and dumped material including syringes, but this is historical reporting and does not establish current hazards. A 2021 report said little evidence of the zoo remained. A private crematorium proposal for the Symonston site was conditionally approved and then challenged in ACAT in 2024; no current construction status was confirmed. Private land: no entry or approach beyond public roads. Treat any residual debris as potentially unsafe; current site hazards have not been surveyed publicly. Checked 26 Nov 2026. Sources: https://region.com.au/ghost-zoo-the-wreckage-on-mugga-lane/8028/ ; https://region.com.au/plans-lodged-for-private-crematorium-on-south-side/494709/ ; https://region.com.au/group-faces-legal-hurdle-in-bid-to-overturn-crematorium-approval/734943/ ; https://www.acat.act.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0005/2460443/COLLETT-and-ORS-v-ACT-PLANNING-AND-LAND-AUTHORITY-2024-ACAT-39.pdf

name: Former NAB / Kowalski Offices — London Circuit
area: Civic — London Circuit / Ainslie Place public frontage; public footpaths only.
status: Former commercial premises — neglect and broken windows reported; redevelopment approved; current vacancy and construction status unverified
notes: The former NAB and Kowalski Recruitment premises are documented at the London Circuit / Ainslie Place frontage. A 2025 development report described an approved office redevelopment/consolidation proposal. A December 2025 community post reported smashed windows, while a 2 Nov 2026 photograph shows the former NAB building still standing. No authoritative current occupancy or construction update was located, so this is not confirmed abandoned. View only from public footpaths; do not enter or touch possible broken glass. Checked 26 Nov 2026. name: Cowper Street Houses — Dickson (Unverified Vacancy Report)
area: Dickson — Cowper Street general area; exact residential addresses and pins withheld.
status: Unverified historical vacancy report — a redevelopment proposal sought demolition of five dwellings; present status not confirmed
notes: A February 2024 community post described several apparently vacant houses on Cowper Street. Separately, DA 202341375 proposed demolition of five existing dwellings and a 22-apartment supportive-housing development; later planning/traffic documents indicate works planning, but the current demolition and construction status was not independently verified. Do not treat the houses as currently abandoned. These are private residential blocks: do not visit, approach residents, or publish individual addresses. Occupancy and hazards are unknown. Checked 26 Nov 2026. Sources: https://www.reddit.com/r/canberra/comments/1alfqsq ; https://www.planningalerts.org.au/applications/2913888 ; https://dafinder.blob.core.windows.net/dadocuments/DOCs/SCRITERIA-202341375-01.pdf

name: Honeysuckle Creek Tracking Station
area: Namadgi National Park — Honeysuckle Campground visitor area.
status: Decommissioned space-tracking station — surviving remnants at an official public campground; historic site, not an abandoned building
notes: The former tracking station supported the Apollo-era space program; Parks ACT confirms remnants remain near Honeysuckle Campground. Public access is through the official campground and signed visitor areas; campground bookings and park rules apply. Do not climb or interfere with remnants. Remote alpine conditions, changing weather and unreliable mobile reception are hazards; bring water and check park alerts before travel. Checked 26 Nov 2026. Source: https://www.parks.act.gov.au/find-a-nature-park/namadgi-national-park/honeysuckle-campground

name: Orroral Valley Tracking Station
area: Namadgi National Park — designated Orroral Tracking Station visitor area.
status: Decommissioned tracking station — historic infrastructure and interpretation remain; official visitor access available
notes: The former tracking station is a separate site from Orroral Homestead. ACT Government reopened vehicle access to the Orroral Tracking Station and Orroral Heritage Walk on 27 May 2023. Use only the designated visitor area and public tracks; do not enter or climb structures. The valley is remote, mobile reception is unreliable, and road/track conditions can change; check Parks ACT alerts and conditions first. Checked 26 Nov 2026. Sources: https://www.cmtedd.act.gov.au/open_government/inform/act_government_media_releases/gentleman/2023/areas-of-orroral-valley-reopening ; https://www.parks.act.gov.au/find-a-nature-park/namadgi-national-park/orroral-campground

name: Demandering Hut — Fire-damaged Ruins
area: Southern Namadgi National Park — general sector only; exact location and approach withheld.
status: Verified heritage hut ruins — destroyed in the 2020 Orroral Valley fire; fenced-off remains; government decided not to rebuild
notes: Demandering Hut was destroyed in the 2020 Orroral Valley bushfire. ABC reporting in July 2025 documented the burnt stone chimney, charred remains and fenced-off site; in August 2025 the ACT Government confirmed the hut would not be rebuilt. The area is also recognised as significant to First Nations people, so no coordinates, access directions or entry details are published. Do not approach or cross fencing; burnt and unstable debris and remote bushland conditions present hazards. Checked 26 Nov 2026. Sources: https://www.abc.net.au/news/2025-07-13/namadgi-huts-remain-in-ruins-after-black-summer-fires/105521172 ; https://www.abc.net.au/news/2025-08-13/heritage-huts-namadgi-not-rebuilt-oldfield/105642082 ; https://www.act.gov.au/environment/heritage/act-heritage-register ; https://www.npaact.org.au/npaact-news/media-release/act-government-rethink-needed-on-namadgi-huts

name: Max and Bert Oldfields Hut — Fire-damaged Ruins
area: Southern Namadgi National Park — general sector only; exact location and approach withheld.
status: Verified historic hut ruins — destroyed in the 2020 Orroral Valley fire; no replacement planned
notes: Max and Bert Oldfields Hut was destroyed in the 2020 Orroral Valley fire. ABC reporting in 2025 records the remaining ruins and the ACT Government decision not to rebuild. The surrounding area has recognised First Nations cultural significance; exact location, coordinates and directions are intentionally withheld. Do not seek out or enter the ruins; burnt debris and remote alpine conditions are unsafe. Checked 26 Nov 2026. Sources: https://www.abc.net.au/news/2025-07-13/namadgi-huts-remain-in-ruins-after-black-summer-fires/105521172 ; https://www.abc.net.au/news/2025-08-13/heritage-huts-namadgi-not-rebuilt-oldfield/105642082 ; https://www.npaact.org.au/npaact-news/media-release/act-government-rethink-needed-on-namadgi-huts

name: Bobeyan Homestead Ruins
area: Southern Namadgi National Park — Boboyan Valley; general heritage area only, no precise pin.
status: Historic pastoral homestead ruins — publicly documented on the official Old Boboyan Road heritage walk
notes: The former Bobeyan pastoral homestead is represented by surviving ruins and landscape traces. Parks ACT lists the Old Boboyan Road to Boboyan Valley walk as open and identifies the ruins as a heritage feature. This is a remote, exposed walking area; stay on the official route, do not disturb masonry, graves or artefacts, and check road conditions and park alerts. Exact site coordinates are not published because of the remote cultural landscape. Checked 26 Nov 2026. name: Lone Pine Homestead Ruins
area: Southern Namadgi National Park — Boboyan Valley / Grassy Creek area; exact location and approach withheld.
status: Historic pastoral homestead ruin — stone chimney and foundation remnants documented; remote site
notes: Lone Pine (also called Lonesome Pine) was a pastoral homestead in the southern Namadgi landscape. Heritage and archival material documents the ruin and surviving chimney/foundation traces. It lies in a remote cultural landscape close to the ACT–NSW border; this record is limited to the ACT-side general area and does not publish coordinates or directions. Do not leave official public tracks or disturb masonry, plantings or possible graves. Remote terrain, creek crossings, cold weather and unreliable reception are hazards. Checked 26 Nov 2026. name: Tin Dish School / Bobeyan Subsidised School Ruins
area: Southern Namadgi National Park — Settlers Track / Bobeyan Valley general area; no precise pin.
status: Verified archaeological school-site remains — school closed in 1910; only small structural traces remain
notes: The one-room Bobeyan Subsidised School, known locally as Tin Dish School, operated in the early 1900s and closed in 1910. Hall Heritage Centre records only a few corner posts, post holes and shaped fireplace stones remain. It is an archaeological site, not a standing building. Do not dig, collect objects or disturb the remains; use the official Settlers Track visitor information and remain on public routes. Remote conditions and weather exposure apply. Checked 26 Nov 2026. name: Lutons Crutching Shed
area: Namadgi National Park — Mount Clear / Boboyan Valley general area; exact approach withheld.
status: Historic pastoral shed — standing disused structure; ACT Heritage Council considered but did not provisionally register it
notes: Built in the 1960s for sheep crutching, the corrugated-iron shed was later altered for possible ranger use but that use did not proceed. The ACT Heritage Council's 2019 background report places it within Namadgi National Park and records access from a locked gate; no route or gate details are reproduced here. The Kosciuszko Huts Association describes the structure as being in good condition. Do not bypass gates or enter the shed; remote terrain, weather and unreliable phone coverage are hazards. Checked 26 Nov 2026. name: Brayshaw's Homestead — Restored Historic Hut
area: Southern Namadgi National Park — official Settlers Track visitor route.
status: Historic pastoral hut — restored and maintained; publicly viewable from the heritage track; not abandoned
notes: Built in 1903 for the Brayshaw family, the hut was occupied until the early 1960s and later used as shearers' quarters. It was extensively restored in the late 1980s and is now a preserved heritage structure on the Settlers Track. Do not enter unless officially permitted or disturb the fabric; stay on the signed track. Remote walking conditions, weather and unreliable reception apply. Checked 26 Nov 2026. Sources: https://www.parks.act.gov.au/things-to-do/historic-huts ; https://khuts.org/index.php/huts/namadgi-national-park-huts/david-brayshaws-hut ; https://www.act.gov.au/environment/heritage/act-heritage-register

name: Westerman's Homestead — Restored Historic Site
area: Southern Namadgi National Park — official Settlers Track visitor route.
status: Historic pastoral homestead — surviving buildings conserved; public heritage-track site; not abandoned
notes: The Westerman family established the Lons Vale homestead in the 1880s and lived there for decades. The surviving homestead is one of the historic places on the Settlers Track and is managed as a heritage site, not an abandoned building. View from the designated route, respect nearby graves and do not enter closed structures. Remote conditions, weather and unreliable reception apply. Checked 26 Nov 2026. Sources: https://www.parks.act.gov.au/things-to-do/historic-huts ; https://www.parks.act.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0005/404591/the-settlers-track-self-guided-walk.pdf ; https://www.parks.act.gov.au/find-a-nature-park/namadgi-national-park/namadgi-national-park-walking-tracks

name: Waterhole Hut — Restored Historic Hut
area: Southern Namadgi National Park — Settlers Track public walking route; no precise pin.
status: Historic 1939 stockman's hut — restored and in good condition; not abandoned
notes: Waterhole Hut was built in 1939 to support grazing and later restored by the Kosciuszko Huts Association in 2004–05. Parks ACT includes it on the Settlers Track. The hut is a heritage structure, not an abandoned building. Do not damage, enter closed areas or disturb nearby stockyards; remote walking, weather and creek conditions can be hazardous. Checked 26 Nov 2026. name: Horse Gully Hut / John Lennane's Hut Remains
area: Southern Namadgi National Park — official Naas Valley to Horse Gully Hut walking route.
status: Historic hut and earlier hut remains — current hut maintained for walkers/emergency shelter; not abandoned
notes: Parks ACT identifies Horse Gully Hut as a heritage-listed hut on the Naas Valley track. The current hut dates from the 1940s; remnants of the earlier John Lennane's Hut remain nearby. The official walk is 16 km return from Mt Clear Campground and includes several creek crossings. Stay on the route, follow the hut code, bring water and check conditions; remote terrain and unreliable reception are hazards. Checked 26 Nov 2026. name: Orroral Homestead and Shearing Shed
area: Orroral Valley, Namadgi National Park — official Orroral Heritage Walk.
status: Conserved historic pastoral homestead — standing heritage site with public walking access; not abandoned
notes: The Orroral Homestead is a surviving pastoral-era building near Orroral Campground; the associated shearing shed dates from around 1930. Parks ACT identifies the homestead as a heritage stop and the Orroral Heritage Walk is open. Use designated paths only; do not climb or enter closed structures. Remote conditions, weather, creek/water hazards and unreliable mobile reception apply. Checked 26 Nov 2026. name: Palmerville Historic Settlement Remains
area: Evatt — Palmerville Heritage Park, Owen Dixon Drive; public park.
status: Verified archaeological remains in a public heritage park — no standing village buildings
notes: Palmerville was a substantial rural settlement occupied from 1829 to 1959. The former Ginninderra Store and Post Office, Ginninderra Cottage, woolshed and residential complex are represented by archaeological remains, mounds, shallow depressions and surface building debris. The park is open daily with interpretive signs and public walking/picnic facilities. Uneven ground and surface debris may cause trips; do not dig, remove artefacts or disturb remains. Checked 26 Nov 2026. Source: https://www.canberratracks.act.gov.au/heritage-trails/track-6-belconnen/palmerville

name: Kambah Homestead Site
area: Kambah — Adventure Playground / Laidlaw Place public recreation area.
status: Former homestead demolished — tennis-court traces and orchard/windbreak plantings remain; public park
notes: The former 600-acre Kambah sheep and cattle property once had a homestead and pool near the Adventure Playground. The house and pool are gone; remnants of the tennis court and old orchard/windbreak trees remain. Canberra Tracks lists the site as open daily. Use public park areas only; uneven ground and old landscape remnants may be trip hazards. Checked 26 Nov 2026. Source: https://www.canberratracks.act.gov.au/heritage-trails/track-8-tuggeranong-heritage-track/kambah-homestead-site

name: Kambah Woolshed
area: Kambah — public picnic shelter at O'Halloran Circuit / Springbett Street.
status: Historic woolshed — greatly altered and reused as a public picnic/BBQ shelter; not abandoned
notes: This is one of the few surviving buildings from the Kambah property. The former slab-hut area is now a community garden and the old woolshed is used as a covered public picnic/BBQ area. Canberra Tracks lists it as open daily; bookings may be required for groups. Use public facilities, respect bookings and do not climb or damage historic fabric. Checked 26 Nov 2026. Source: https://www.canberratracks.act.gov.au/heritage-trails/track-8-tuggeranong-heritage-track/kambah-woolshed

name: Urambi Homestead Site
area: Kambah — Urambi Hill Nature Reserve / Learmonth Drive public walking area.
status: Former homestead demolished — scattered farm infrastructure traces remain on a public walking route
notes: The farmhouse, stable and outbuildings at Urambi were demolished. Canberra Tracks records traces including an old tank stand, cement floor and trough of a pigsty, and the site of a sheep dip. A public 4 km walking route circles the base of Urambi. Stay on established paths; uneven terrain, old concrete and remote bushland conditions may be hazardous. Checked 26 Nov 2026. Source: https://www.canberratracks.act.gov.au/heritage-trails/track-8-tuggeranong-heritage-track/urambi-homestead-site

name: Athllon Homestead Site
area: Gowrie — public heritage sign near the Scout Hall, Finlay Place.
status: Former homestead demolished — only a gate post remains; public interpretive stop
notes: The earlier timber homestead burnt in 1952 and its replacement was demolished during Tuggeranong's suburban development. Canberra Tracks says only the gate post remains and identifies a public heritage sign near the Scout Hall in Finlay Place. View from public paths; take care around local roads and do not enter adjoining private property. Checked 26 Nov 2026. Source: https://www.canberratracks.act.gov.au/heritage-trails/track-8-tuggeranong-heritage-track/athllon-homestead-site

name: Cranleigh Homestead Site
area: Latham — public heritage plaque near Real Place; view from public streets only.
status: Historic homestead dismantled — no building remains; orchard plantings and interpretive marker survive
notes: General Legge's Cranleigh house was dismantled and its bricks reused in 1955. Canberra Tracks records surviving apricot and olive plantings and an interpretive plaque near an undeveloped block. View from public streets only; do not enter the block or nearby private property. Vegetation and uneven ground may conceal trip hazards. Checked 26 Nov 2026. Source: https://www.canberratracks.act.gov.au/heritage-trails/track-6-belconnen/cranleigh-homestead-site

name: Sherwood Former Homestead Site
area: Uriarra Creek / Blue Range area, ACT — remote heritage walk; general area only.
status: Heritage-listed former homestead — cottage no longer exists; cemetery and landscape remnants remain
notes: The former Sherwood homestead dates to 1863. Canberra Tracks says the slab cottage is gone; a burial plot later consecrated as an Anglican cemetery remains nearby. The site is a remote walk or ride from Blue Range Recreation Area. Respect the cemetery and graves, stay on established public routes and do not disturb heritage material. Remote terrain and weather exposure are hazards. Checked 26 Nov 2026. Source: https://www.canberratracks.act.gov.au/rural-sites/sherwood

name: Ginninderra Blacksmith's Workshop
area: Nicholls / Gold Creek area — exact pin and approach withheld; use official visitor information only.
status: Heritage-listed historic workshop — conservation work recorded in 2013; later described as derelict; current condition/access uncertain
notes: Built around 1860, this is the only surviving ACT building representing a village blacksmith. Canberra Tracks records conservation works in 2013 and an interpretive sign; ABC reporting in 2022 described the neighbouring blacksmith's shop as derelict. The site record also notes an Aboriginal glass artefact, so precise coordinates and directions are withheld. Do not enter fenced areas, touch artefacts or disturb the site; possible structural deterioration is unassessed. Checked 26 Nov 2026. Sources: https://www.canberratracks.act.gov.au/heritage-trails/track-5-gungahlin/ginninderra-blacksmiths-workshop ; https://www.abc.net.au/news/2022-03-27/canberra-homestead-demolished-to-remove-asbestos/100941750 ; https://www.act.gov.au/environment/heritage/act-heritage-register

name: Deasland Homestead — Demolished Site
area: Gold Creek / Nicholls area — former homestead land on private property; exact location withheld.
status: Heritage-listed homestead demolished in March 2022 due to Mr Fluffy loose-fill asbestos; associated structures retained privately
notes: The 1893 Deasland homestead was demolished in March 2022 under the ACT asbestos response. ABC reporting says the historic brick dairy, machinery shed and tennis court were required to remain on the property. The land was sold to a private buyer and a new dwelling was planned; current land use and condition are unverified. Private property: no public access and no exact pin. The demolition was asbestos-related; do not assume remaining land or structures are safe. Checked 26 Nov 2026. Sources: https://www.abc.net.au/news/2022-03-27/canberra-homestead-demolished-to-remove-asbestos/100941750 ; https://www.act.gov.au/environment/heritage/act-heritage-register

name: Former Ginninderra Police Station — Fire-destroyed Site
area: Gold Creek / Nicholls area — general area only; exact site location withheld.
status: Historic police-station building destroyed by suspicious fire in April 2024; current remnants/cleanup status unverified
notes: Local reporting on 4 April 2024 said a historic building believed to be part of the former Ginninderra Police Station was destroyed by a suspicious fire after partially collapsing. No current official update on remaining debris or redevelopment was located. The exact location is withheld because the site is within a private heritage precinct. Do not approach or enter; fire-damaged structures and debris can be unstable. Checked 26 Nov 2026. Source: https://www.onsceneact.com.au/index.php/696-historic-gold-creek-building-destroyed-following-suspicious-blaze-overnight

name: Former Canberra PCYC Community Hub — Turner
area: Turner — former Watson Street PCYC site; public-road view only; active redevelopment.
status: Former derelict building demolished in September 2025; 55-unit housing project reached topping-out milestone in May 2026
notes: The storm-damaged former PCYC headquarters became derelict before demolition began on 23 September 2025. CHC reported the 55-unit social and affordable housing project reached its topping-out milestone on 7 May 2026, with completion expected in early 2027. This is no longer an abandoned building. Active construction site: stay outside hoarding and follow all traffic and site-safety signs. Checked 26 Nov 2026. Sources: https://chcaustralia.com.au/55-new-social-and-affordable-homes-a-step-closer-as-cpcyc-project-tops-out/ ; https://www.snowfoundation.org.au/news/turner-site-topping-out-a-milestone-worth-celebrating/ ; https://www.snowfoundation.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/Media-Release-Turner-CPCYC-Demolition.pdf

name: The Valley Ruin
area: Gungahlin — public heritage viewing area near Gungahlin Drive / The Valley Avenue; no entry into the ruin.
status: Verified standing pastoral ruin — three phases of dwelling construction remain visible; public heritage stop, not an active building
notes: The Gribble family settled here in the 1860s. A slab hut was followed by a pisé addition in 1874–78 and a stone house in 1887; Canberra Tracks says all three phases remain visible. The site is listed as an open daily heritage stop. View from public areas only; do not climb or enter the ruin. Uneven ground, fragile masonry and nearby road traffic are hazards. Checked 26 Nov 2026. Source: https://www.canberratracks.act.gov.au/heritage-trails/track-5-gungahlin/the-valley-ruin

name: Crinigan's Hut Ruin
area: Amaroo — Crinigan Park, Ling Place; public park.
status: Verified archaeological dwelling ruin — excavated and stabilised for public interpretation; not an intact or habitable building
notes: Crinigan's Hut is described by Canberra Tracks as the only remaining small Ginninderra dwelling. The Canberra Archaeological Society excavated and secured the ruin so visitors can learn about the mid-to-late-1800s household; part of the original orchard survives. Open daily as a public park. Do not climb, dig, remove objects or disturb the archaeology; uneven ground and fragile remains are hazards. Checked 26 Nov 2026. Source: https://www.canberratracks.act.gov.au/heritage-trails/track-5-gungahlin/crinigans-hut

name: Mulligans Flat Schools Site
area: Forde — Mulligans Flat Nature Reserve, near the designated visitor carpark; public reserve.
status: Historic school-site remains — no school building survives; brick/stone mound and planted pines remain
notes: The first school was a slab hut built in 1896 and was later replaced by a weatherboard building removed in 1933. Canberra Tracks records two rows of radiata pines planted by pupils in 1920 and a small mound of brick and stone where the chimney stood. The site is in the public nature reserve and is open daily. Stay on visitor paths, do not disturb the mound or remove artefacts; uneven ground and reserve conditions are hazards. Checked 26 Nov 2026. Source: https://www.canberratracks.act.gov.au/heritage-trails/track-5-gungahlin/mulligans-flat-schools

name: Tralee Slab Hut
area: Hume — Tralee Street public-road frontage; hut is fenced off and not accessible.
status: Restored 19th-century slab hut — repaired in 2011; currently fenced off; visible from public land at a distance
notes: The late-1800s slab hut demonstrates vertical and horizontal slab construction. ACT-funded repairs using period-appropriate timber skills were completed in 2011. Canberra Tracks currently says the site is fenced off and inaccessible, with the hut visible from about 50 metres away. Do not cross the fence or attempt entry. The nearby Hume industrial area has vehicle and worksite traffic. Checked 26 Nov 2026. Source: https://www.canberratracks.act.gov.au/heritage-trails/track-8-tuggeranong-heritage-track/tralee-slab-hut

name: Stromlo Forestry Settlement
area: Duffy — Forestry Street / former Stromlo Forestry Settlement; private homes, general area only.
status: Historic forestry settlement — 2003 bushfires destroyed 17 homes and forestry buildings; three older houses survive as private residences
notes: The settlement developed from the late 1920s through 1972 to house forestry workers and support the forestry depot. Canberra Tracks records that the 2003 fires destroyed 17 homes and all other forestry-associated buildings; only three older houses survived. These are private residences, not urbex sites. No house numbers, coordinates or directions are published. View the historic settlement only from public roads; do not approach or photograph residents. Checked 26 Nov 2026. Source: https://www.canberratracks.act.gov.au/heritage-trails/track-7-woden-heritage-track/stromlo-forestry-settlement

name: Gungaderra Historic Homestead and Machinery Shed
area: Harrison — Mapleton Avenue community precinct; use advertised public/community access only.
status: Historic pastoral complex — homestead and machinery shed survive and are in community use; not abandoned
notes: Gungaderra began as a slab hut in 1861. The 1902–04 homestead and 1911–13 machinery shed survive with historic plantings. Canberra Tracks says the site is managed by CHC Affordable Housing and now hosts playgroups, exhibitions and a men's shed. It is an active community site, not an abandoned building. Respect program hours and do not enter private or closed areas. Checked 26 Nov 2026. Source: https://www.canberratracks.act.gov.au/heritage-trails/track-5-gungahlin/gungaderra

name: Well Station Historic Farm and Track
area: Harrison — Nullarbor Avenue public walking track; old farm buildings are not confirmed as public-access interiors.
status: Historic pastoral farm — surviving old farm and outbuildings beside a public heritage walking track; current building occupancy unverified
notes: The late-1800s Well Station track connected the farms of Well Station and Gungaderra. Canberra Tracks describes surviving old farm buildings alongside newer Harrison development and lists the walking track as open daily. This does not grant access to the farm buildings or paddocks. Stay on the public track and do not enter structures or private land; current occupancy and structural condition are unverified. Checked 26 Nov 2026. Source: https://www.canberratracks.act.gov.au/heritage-trails/track-5-gungahlin/well-station-track

name: Belconnen Naval Transmitting Station (Former HMAS Belconnen)
area: Lawson North — former Commonwealth defence site; general area only; public access prohibited.
status: Decommissioned defence communications site — last transmission 17 June 2005; towers felled in 2006; remaining site off-limits and subject to redevelopment/land management
notes: Built in 1938–39, the Royal Australian Naval Transmitting Station (also known as HMAS Belconnen or 'Bells') was a major naval wireless facility. The final message was sent on 17 June 2005; the transmitter towers were felled in December 2006. Canberra Tracks explicitly says the former site is off limits to the public. Defence and National Capital Authority documents describe Commonwealth land, heritage/ecological constraints and past decontamination requirements; parts of Lawson North have been proposed for Defence housing redevelopment. Do not enter, approach fences or attempt to locate remaining equipment. Potential contamination, protected grassland, active development and restricted defence land are hazards. Exact location, coordinates and access details withheld. Checked 26 Nov 2026. Sources: https://www.canberratracks.act.gov.au/heritage-trails/track-6-belconnen/naval-transmitting-station ; https://navyhistory.au/naval-heritage-sites/royal-australian-naval-transmitting-station-act/ ; https://www.dcceew.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/72181.pdf ; https://www.nca.gov.au/sites/default/files/DCP-1209-Block-2-Section-6-Block-1-Section-16%20-Lawson-%20Belconnen-Naval-Transmitting%20Station-Consultation-Report.pdf ; https://region.com.au/lawson-defence-housing-project-site-halved-but-conservationists-vow-to-fight-on/740436/
